source.title: Generalization by Recognizing Confusion
source.authors: Daniel Chiu; Franklyn Wang; S. Kominers

page_placements.theme: Example-specific memorization can help valid rare or difficult examples

record.file_problem: The supplied full text appears complete; no garbling or cutoff noted.
record.tranche_reason: Tests a related random-label fitting behavior using self-adaptive training and reports results; this differs from the original standard-network training setup.
record.gate_note: The paper tests self-adaptive training on random labels and reports its training accuracy/generalization gap and posterior behavior. It also tests class imbalance, which does not match the listed versions. The standard-network random-label results in the introduction are attributed to prior work, so they are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The authors directly measure fitting of entirely random CIFAR-10 labels using self-adaptive training. This tests dependence on the training procedure, but does not reproduce V1's standard, unchanged training recipe.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately describes the authors' random-label conclusion: self-adaptive methods fail to fit random labels, which they interpret as evidence suggesting low empirical Rademacher complexity. This is preliminary evidence, not a complexity bound or proof of generalization. Their broader conclusion also emphasizes improved noisy-label classification with mixup and a tradeoff with rare-class recognition.
record.recipe_differences: Uses self-adaptive training, which changes labels and reweights examples during training; the random-label experiment follows the cited self-adaptive-training procedure rather than the original standard SGD recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Label correction begins at epoch 60 in the class-imbalance experiment; after it begins, minority-class accuracy decreases, drastically for r ∈ {24, 99}.

fits_no_version.finding: Adaptive soft labels converge to approximately uniform class probabilities, reported as 10% ± 0.2% per class.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Self-adaptive training responds to fully random labels by making its adaptive targets nearly uniform.

fits_no_version.finding: Self-adaptive training reduces minority-class test accuracy relative to vanilla cross-entropy after label correction begins, especially at class ratios 24 and 99.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive label correction can sacrifice rare-class recognition under class imbalance.

record.problems: The random-label experiment is not the standard-network setup named in the claim. The number of runs is described only as several, with no uncertainty interval. The reported generalization gap is not a direct report of chance test error. The class-imbalance results are shown only in a figure without numeric values in the text.

untested.parts: Independent reproduction with standard training and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters; the perfect-fitting reference column does not document such an experiment.
Relative fitting time and convergence as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian inputs.
Perfect training fit together with steadily worsening test performance across the full corruption range. Table 1 reports mitigation performance without corresponding training-fit measurements.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and conventional data augmentation on random-label fitting, and generalization after removing them. Adaptive label correction does not establish these comparisons.
Original measurements showing real patterns learned before noise. Figure 1 and its associated learning-order evidence are reproduced from prior work.

record.verdict_notes: Table 3 explicitly states chance test accuracy. Its generic perfect-fitting reference column should not be treated as a newly measured standard-training result. The main extraction error reverses the random-label experiment by assigning that reference column's 100.0% accuracy to self-adaptive training.

versions.untested_parts: Tests self-adaptive training on CIFAR-10 with entirely random labels; does not test standard networks trained without self-adaptive training or establish the original standard-network recipe.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet 34x10 boosted with self-adaptive training
rows.operation_detail: trained on CIFAR-10 with entirely random labels using self-adaptive training
rows.note: Table reports random-label training accuracy under self-adaptive training.
rows.check: Wrong table column: SAT and self-adaptive mixup have 10.2% training accuracy, not 100.0%. The 100.0% entry belongs to the generic reference column for models that fit training data perfectly. Table 3 groups SAT and the authors' mixup variant together.

source_check.correct: Self-adaptive training and self-adaptive mixup (alpha = 0.2) have 10.2% training accuracy and 10% test accuracy. The 100.0% training accuracy belongs to the generic reference column for models that fit training data perfectly. The absent state agrees with the corrected value.
source_check.problem: Training accuracy was taken from the wrong table column.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet 34x10 boosted with self-adaptive training
rows.operation_detail: trained on CIFAR-10 with entirely random labels using self-adaptive training
rows.note: The reported generalization gap does not itself state test error at chance; the text separately says predicted class for all test images is identical.
rows.check: The 0.2 percentage-point gap is correct. Table 3 explicitly gives 10% test accuracy and 10.2% training accuracy, establishing chance-level performance on both. The table groups SAT and self-adaptive mixup together.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet 34x10 boosted with self-adaptive training
rows.operation_detail: measured soft-label posterior probabilities after random-label training
rows.measure: Per-example probability of each of 10 classes
rows.value: 10% ± 0.2% probability of being in each of the 10 classes
rows.note: Authors state soft labels converge to almost exactly uniform probabilities irrespective of initial labels.
rows.check: Uniform soft-label probabilities measure the adaptive targets, not classification accuracy against the original random labels. This row alone cannot establish whether those labels are fitted.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet 34x10

rows.note: Text says self-adaptive training is inferior in the imbalanced-class regime and minority-class accuracy decreases after label correction, but supplies no exact values.
rows.check: Minority-class test accuracy under class imbalance does not measure any listed version. The supplied figure contains no readable numerical curves.

relationships.condition: Wide ResNet-34x10 on entirely random CIFAR-10 labels with self-adaptive training, including the self-adaptive mixup variant
